URL: https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/trump-iraq-military-exit-b3059282.html
The Independent (Associated Press, Qassim Abdul-Zahra) — published 2026-09-30T18:15:35Z

The US military said Wednesday it completed the withdrawal of all American troops from Iraq after the final service members left an air base in northern Iraq under a deal between Baghdad and Washington, ending a 12-year mission against the Islamic State group.
QUOTE (Donald Trump, Truth Social): the end of "a very expensive excursion into Hell"; described the drawdown ahead of a Sept 30 deadline as "orderly"; "It has been a long time, with very bad decision-making that got us involved in this quagmire in the first place, but soon, that will be part of History."
QUOTE (Trump, White House Hispanic Heritage Month event, Wednesday): "It's been a long time with very bad decision making that got us involved in this quagmire in the first place. It was a quagmire. For many, many years it lasted. But soon that part of history will be over."
QUOTE (Trump, same event): "It's a victory for the United States, it's a victory for Iraq and a decisive victory over ISIS, which has been completely decimated."
QUOTE (Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell): "This milestone reflects the success of a 12-year campaign that defeated ISIS as an organized military threat in Iraq and across the region." / "It also marks a transition from a wartime coalition mission to an Iraqi-led security effort supported by a more normal bilateral security relationship." He added the US military "will continue to provide targeted training and intelligence support to our Iraqi partners."
QUOTE (Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, presiding over the handover ceremony): the withdrawal is the beginning of a "new phase, one defined by Iraq's sovereignty, the strength of its institutions, the readiness of its forces, the unity of its decision-making, and balanced partnerships with its friends."
The last troops left the air base in Irbil (Erbil), in northern Iraq's semi-autonomous Kurdish region.
US troops invaded Iraq in 2003 to topple Saddam Hussein; departed in 2011; returned three years later at Iraqi invitation to fight Islamic State. Washington and Baghdad agreed in 2024 to wind the mission down.
Iraq's government initially linked the Sept 30 withdrawal deadline to disarmament of non-state armed groups; al-Zaidi has since pushed the militia-disarmament deadline to June 2027 (told the New York Times earlier this month).
NOT YET SOURCED IN AN APPROVED OUTLET: US CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper's statement handing "full primary responsibility for Iraq's security" to the Iraqi government (seen via thehill.com); al-Zaidi's declaration of 1 October as "Sovereignty Day" (seen via dw.com); Trump's line "I had a choice to stay or to leave, and felt, without question, that it was time for America to go home!" (seen via euronews.com / middle-east-online.com). centcom.mil and whitehouse.gov are approved domains — check those for primaries.
